paragraphs:

When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard. Within the first hour, checkpoints on the outskirts of the remote desert city nestled among the rocky hills of northern Mali had fallen to the insurgents, who pushed towards the police station where fierce fighting erupted.

“Everything was happening at once. Explosions were going off all around us, people were shouting,” recalled a former member of Russia’s Africa Corps who was stationed in Mali at the time and spoke on condition of anonymity. “Nobody knew where the enemy was coming from.”

articles.summary:

paragraphs:

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

Australia is nearly on track to reach its 2030 emissions reduction target but will fall massively short of a 2035 target unless the federal government substantially ramps up its climate policies, according to new official projections.

Under existing policies, the country is on track by 2035 to cut climate pollution by only 48% compared with 2005 levels – far below its target reduction of between 62% and 70% by that date, climate department projections suggest.

articles.title: Brussels on split-screen: where it flexes – and where it bends
articles.summary:

•
paragraphs:
From a choreographed summit that dominated Westminster but barely registered in Brussels to a climate showdown in Turkey, last week revealed the EU’s priorities – and the limits of its collective power

• Don’t get This Is Europe delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

Two very different European diplomatic dramas played out almost simultaneously last week. On Friday, a tightly choreographed EU-UK summit transfixed London, while barely registering on the continent. On Sunday, Cop31 collapsed after a united EU forcefully vetoed a watered-down climate pact, even as it relaxed its own green rules at home.

What do these two events reveal about the EU: how it works, what takes up its bandwidth, how it exercises its clout – and where it’s vulnerable?
